summary: Traverse nodes and edges (or grid cells) using BFS for shortest-path/level-order needs or DFS for connectivity/exhaustive exploration.
recognize_when: input is an adjacency list/matrix or an implicit grid of cells
need shortest path in an unweighted graph (use BFS)
need to find connected components, cycles, or explore all paths (use DFS)
need topological order or to detect cycles in a directed graph

complexity.notes: each vertex and edge visited once; space covers visited set, queue/stack, and recursion depth for DFS

gotchas: marking a node visited when it's popped instead of when it's enqueued causes duplicate queue entries in BFS
forgetting to check grid bounds before visiting a neighbor cell
using DFS recursion on very deep/large graphs can hit Python's recursion limit; consider an explicit stack
not handling disconnected components when a single traversal from one start node won't cover the whole graph
